cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: A Necessary Heartbreak
cards.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'm sorry I broke your graduation mug. Losing it is exactly how we learn to let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That urge is why we needed this. We've confused a degree with a drinking vessel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then give me your graduation mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Losing mine will teach me generosity. We should both drink from jam jars tomorrow.

mechanism: A makes granting repair permission depend on accepting loss as growth, then accepts an equivalent lesson personally.
confusable: Unlike avoiding responsibility with cheerfulness, A explicitly calls the unwanted loss necessary and applies it to self.
comparison: Reciprocal domestic loss tests A's philosophy personally, unlike the bakery's practical pressure.
seedUse: Use both graduation mugs and jam-jar replacement from the seed; make permission to repair and take the mug drive the hierarchy.
